text: My guards were still looking for me this morning. That's why I've been so far.
Give me your message.
Oh, yes. The warning was too late.
What do you do now? Go back to your friends? The Doctor?
Oh, I can't. He's dead. I saw his body lying in the street by the Abbott's house.
Before I could do anything, Roger Culver saw me and sent the guards after me again.
Heaven knows what I do now.
Turn to England?
England? I can't. I've got to find the key to the TARDIS.
The Doctor has a special key. Without it, I can't leave.
Well, do you know where it is?
The Doctor had it with him, and I'm lost. I don't have time to look for it.
My only hope is that it's still with his own clothes.
What's the episode?
It would have had to change before he went there.
The other place I think he's been to is the shop.
Oh, but we've already searched there, Monsieur, looking for clothes here.
And we must do it again. Please help me.
Open every cupboard. Every box. I must find that key.
It may hinder the inquiry into the attempted assassination of de Coligny.
Surely the King is insisting that de Coligny is avenged.
It is.
But by blaming the death of the Abbott on the Huguenots, we may be able to cover our tracks.
Did the King pay any attention to the Abbott's death?
I don't know.
Fortunately, the Admiral himself is helping us. He doesn't want the inquiry yet.
So that may give us a little time.
Therefore, the Englishman must be caught.
And killed. He must not be allowed to get back to the Abbott's house.
The men are searching Paris for him.
He must be found tonight.
Tomorrow is St. Bartholomew's Day, and it'll be all too easy for him to evade us in the revelry.
Queen Mother wants me to go to her.
No doubt she has thought of some further scheme to protect her good name.
Wait for me here, Simon. I may have more instructions for you when I get back.
Well...
Nothing, Monsieur. There's no sign of your friend's clothes.
He must be here.
He must be here.
All I found was this.
But this is his stick.
Your friend?
Yes. Well, these clothes must be here somewhere. Where did you find this?
In the back, Monsieur. But there are no clothes there.
Are you sure?
Yes. I've searched everywhere.
And why the stick? He couldn't have pretended to be the Abbott dressed as he was.
He must have changed somewhere. But where?
Perhaps he went away somewhere with the apothecary who used to live here.
What, with the prisoner?
No, he couldn't have.
Why not?
Because the prisoner is either dead or in prison.
He is not.
Catholics will not rest until you are dead.
The King is determined to prevent a further attempt.
Why else do you think he will throw heavy a guard on this house?
A Catholic guard under a Catholic commander?
The Admiral could hardly be in the care of a greater enemy.
He is under the protection of the King and the Queen Mother.
Gaston!
You're retarding the Admiral. You're doing yourself an injustice.
You'd better return to the room first.
No!
If you were to leave Paris, it would be better for you and for us.
The surgeon said the Admiral must not be moved.
Then may God protect you.
Henry of Navarre realizes how dangerous it is to have such a hot head in his service.
He must be wrong. The Commander wouldn't dare to dismay the King after what has happened.
Let us hope so.
Is there anything you need, Admiral?
You must be grateful that the wounds are not poisoned, so that there is no fear of you dying.
I do not fear death. I only hope we have nothing to fear from my staying.
Oh, my dear boy, had you stayed at the tavern, all this mix-up could have been avoided.
I did stay at the tavern. You didn't turn up.
Yes, well, I was unavoidably delayed.
Never mind that crowd. Come along, let's go. Come along.
Come now, Monsieur. The curfew is wrong.
What? Oh, that wretched curfew is the start of so much trouble.
It would be easy to leave Paris in the morning, Monsieur.
Tomorrow is St. Bartholomew's Day, and everyone will be celebrating.
Well, with all the trouble that's going on, I can't see what they've got to celebrate.
I told you not to get involved.
Look, I tried not to. But the abbot did look like you.
If I hadn't found out about Admiral de Coligny being the sea pecker...
What's that?
I tried to tell you before. Admiral de Coligny is one of the Huguenot leaders.
The Catholics tried to shoot him.
Did you say tomorrow was St. Bartholomew's Day, child?
What year is this, my boy?
I don't know. What difference does it make?
What date is it, child?
Say, Monsieur. August the 23rd.
Yes, yes, yes. I know that. The year. The year.
1572, Monsieur. But surely you know that.
Go home, Anne. You must leave here at once.
Where to go?
Where were you working?
At the abbot's house.
You go back there.
I can't! They'll kill me!
You must leave this shop, child.
Doctor, what's happening?
Oh, please don't interfere.
Now, my dear, there must be somewhere you can stay in Paris.
No, there's only my aunt's place, and they'll kill me there.
Oh, nonsense. Tonight you will be quite safe.
Now, you go carefully through the streets.
Well, what about the curfew?
Well, you've been out for the curfew before, haven't you?
Yes, but the curfew...
Well, you know how to avoid the patrols.
You go back to your aunt to be quite safe.
And you take my advice and stay indoors tomorrow.
Now, do you understand?
It's too dangerous for you to stay here.
Now, off you go, child. Come along.
Off, off, off.
Doctor, I don't think...
Ah, yes, yes, yes.
Goodbye, Monsieur Stephen.
A safe journey.
Doctor, I don't think she should go.
Now, off you go, my child. Off you go.
Bye.
Look, are you sure she'll be all right?
The guards are waiting for her.
My dear Stephen, the Catholics will have other things on their minds tonight.
She will be quite safe.
Now then, you and I must leave Paris at once. Come.
Doctor, what is going on?
There is no time for me to explain.
Come along, boy. Come along.
Dumas.
I apologize. I thought that...
Never mind.
I have it here.
The order signed by the King.
Our plans for tomorrow can go ahead.
God has very little to do with it.
What is this?
The list, Madame.
When those Huguenots are killed, we need have no further fear of a Protestant France.
We have no need of lists, Marshal.
The good people of Paris know their enemies.
They will take care of them.
The good people?
Madame, if you rouse the mob, the innocent will perish with the guilty.
Innocent?
Yes.
Heresy can have no innocence.
France will breathe the pure air after tomorrow.
Ah, Madame, your son-in-law.
Is he to be slaughtered with the others?
Tomorrow, Henry of Navarre will pay for his pretensions to the Crown.
Madame, we must not kill Navarre.
Must not?
Protestant Europe will merely shed a pious tear at the death of a few thousand Huguenots.
The death of a prince will launch a holy war.
If one Huguenot life escapes you,
we may both regret this act of mercy.
Not mercy, Madame.
Policy.
Very well, Marshal.
Then you must get him out of Paris.
After tomorrow, even I could not save him.
Have a seat with Madame.
And, Marshal, close the gates of the city now.
Well, my Lord, the order has been given.
You may forgive me.
My men are ready.
Where's the lift?
There is no lift.
But I thought...
We are to unleash the wolves of Paris.
None out of his paradise.
Even better, my Lord.
I wonder.
And, Simon, when you have passed on the order, I have a special charge for you.
My Lord.
Henry of Navarre.
I am to have the honor.
Yes, but not of killing him.
You will escort him out of Paris.
But, my Lord.
You will be responsible for his safety.
You will have to leave tomorrow's work to others.
Now, get out.
On tomorrow, the city will weep tears of blood.
It's nearly dawn.
How many more nights have we got to watch over this Huguenot's house?
Till the king decrees otherwise.
Why does it have to be us?
We take a moment.
We just wait.
We'll be sorry to see the night over.
Hello?
What's this?
War, as I expect.
Shall we leave?
Go back to your quarters.
We leave, sir.
It's not due for an hour or more.
No.
We'll guard you.
Go quickly.
Go soon.
It'll be late.
I know.
I know.
Just keep quiet.
Who are the parts of France?
They all die.
The Admiral?
Whether she needn't have died.
But, no.
You had to leave her there to be slaughtered.
Well, it is possible.
Of course, she didn't die.
The girl was already hunted by the Catholic guards.
If they killed 10,000, how did they spare her?
You can't say for certain that you weren't responsible for that girl's death.
To her aunt's house, where the guards were waiting to catch her.
I tell you this much, Doctor.
Wherever this machine of yours lands next, I'm getting off.
If your researches have so little regard for human life, then I want no part in it.
We've learned that science gives us a terrible job.
And that is because we don't quite truly understand.
Why should we?
After all, we're all too small to realize its final pattern.
Therefore, don't try and judge it from where you stand.
I was right to do as I did.
Yes, that I firmly believe.
Even after all this time, he cannot understand.
I dare not change it.
Well, at least I taught him to take some precautions.
He did remember to look at the scanner before he opened the door.
Could understand.
Not even my little Susan.
And as for Barbara and Chatterton.
They're all too impatient to get back to their own time.
Perhaps I should go home.
Who are you?
Where's the telephone?
What did you say?
The telephone. I've got to ring up.
Oh, pull yourself together, child.
I think you've made a mistake.
Who are you? Are you the police?
Oh, good gracious, of course not.
Well, this is a police box.
It says so outside.
Yes, yes, I know.
But it isn't.
If you know what I mean, I'll run along and find another police box.
In any case, child, what do you want to do with the police?
There's been an accident.
A little boy's been hurt, and I've got to phone the police.
Oh, well, I'm afraid I can't help you.
No, you must run along and phone the police, somebody else.
And at the same time, phone for an ambulance.
Wait a minute.
If this isn't a police box, what is it?
And who are you?
Well, my dear, I'm a doctor of science.
And this machine is for traveling through time and relative dimensions in space.
Now, you...
Oh, my dear.
Oh, never mind, my dear.
Never mind.
Run along.
There's something odd going on.
Oh, please, child.
Quick.
You've got to take off.
Oh, should you come back, my boy?
Yes, yes, I'll come back.
We can't go into that now.
There are two policemen coming over the common towards the dark.
Come in here.
They want to use the telephone.
Thank you.
Thank you.
That was close.
Very true.
Tell me, young man, what made you change your mind?
Hmm?
How did you get in here?
Oh, me feet.
Same as you did.
You realize what?
Huh?
We've taken off.
We could land anywhere.
We're really traveling.
We're traveling in time and space.
Oh, we could land anywhere at any age.
Tell us another one.
What else could I do, dear boy?
You don't want a couple of policemen of all the targets, do you?
You know you're the most inconsistent young man.
Just now, you were telling me off for not having a shopping girl of all.
Oh, that was different.
I'm sorry.
Oh, this is no joy ride, you know.
You may never get home again.
I don't...
What about your parents?
I haven't got any.
And it would be great.
And she won't care if she never sees me again.
You see, you always fuss about nothing.
She looks rather like my grandchild, Susan.
I guess I've never met your granddaughter.
Oh, no, no, no, no.
No, of course not.
No.
Yes.
But she does, you know.
What is your name, child?
Dorothea, really.
Dorothea Chaplet.
Chaplet?
Yes.
Yes.
Oh, Elizabeth.
You're not French.
Are you?
No, be damned.
...of all the TARDIS, Miss Dorothea Chaplet.
Dodo.
Oh, my dear.
My dear.
Ha, ha, ha.
